Blizzard Adds Beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' Quest to World of Warcraft: Forever
New World of Warcraft Forever patch notes take us to level 30, with a win for Warriors but sad news for Undead Paladins
Tinker, Bard, Illusionist - Blizzard seemingly surveying World of Warcraft: Forever players about never-before-seen classes to add to the game

singleSourced.context: The quest went live in patch 2.1.2 on June 19, 2007, and has been in the game ever since.

singleSourced.key: i had the honor and privilege of bringing
singleSourced.value: I had the honor and privilege of bringing
singleSourced.context: Johnny Cash, the Blizzard Principal Designer who added the quest, posted on X/Twitter, saying "I had the honor and privilege of bringing "Kyle's Gone Missing!" into WoW: Forever.

singleSourced.key: channeled spells do not count as periodics
singleSourced.value: channeled spells do not count as periodics
singleSourced.context: Gnomes, meanwhile, no longer gain any benefits to periodic effects from Eureka (Blizzard notes that "channeled spells do not count as periodics").

Druids lose Tiger's Fury, which will certainly hurt, but they do gain 75% increased Rage from critical strikes in Bear Form and Dire Bear Form, along with attack-power scaling for Swipe that was previously missing.

Lastly, the threat generated by Primal Bite is "roughly doubled."

Hunter gets some redesigned, "more vanilla feeling" icons for Improved Stings and Predator's Edge.

singleSourced.key: since the original spell needed to hit
singleSourced.value: since the original spell needed to hit.
singleSourced.context:
Frost Mages, meanwhile, no longer roll to check resists on the Winter's Chill talent "since the original spell needed to hit."

Protection Paladin loses one-third of its block chance on Redoubt at all levels, maxing out at 20% instead of 30%, but the block chance on Holy Shield goes up from 20% to 30% to compensate.
Most importantly, they now generate 100% increased Rage when landing critical strikes, solving their biggest frustration.

singleSourced.key: to give fury more access to utility and meaningful choices early
singleSourced.value: to give Fury more access to utility and meaningful choices early,
singleSourced.context: Blizzard has moved many talents around the tree "to give Fury more access to utility and meaningful choices early," while freeing up points later to provide more flexibility.

singleSourced.key: a clear path to the middle
singleSourced.value: a clear path to the middle
singleSourced.context: Rounding us out, Protection Warriors have also had a tree reorganization, aimed at giving non-shield users "a clear path to the middle" and allowing Protection to better serve as a secondary spec for PvP.

singleSourced.key: anduin wrynn and many other children unintentionally have hats
singleSourced.value: Anduin Wrynn - and many other children - unintentionally have hats.
singleSourced.context: The most entertaining is that "Anduin Wrynn - and many other children - unintentionally have hats." Blizzard's in the process of taking these away, although personally I think they should keep it in as a random occurrence.
